messages:
Alice Nguyen: Hey team, just got a high-priority customer report — they renamed an Okta group yesterday and a subset of users lost application roles in our app. They say SCIM shows the group still exists (same externalId) but role mapping in the Redwood console no longer applies. Can someone triage?

Diego Ramos: Sorry to hear that. Quick q: did they rename the group name only or change the displayName and externalId?

Alice Nguyen: Only displayName changed from "Billing - North America" to "Billing NA". externalId stayed the same. Okta SCIM logs show a PATCH to /Groups/<id> with new displayName, no members change.

Priya Patel: Hmm. Our group->role matching in console currently supports matching by group name and externalId, but there's a config toggle for preferExternalId=false by default for older customers. If their org still matches by displayName, rename would break mapping until we re-sync.

Alice Nguyen: Customer insists mapping used to survive renames. They have a custom role mapping in the org settings (UI screenshot attached). It shows matching rule: "group.name EQUALS 'Billing - North America' -> role: billing-admin"

Jamie (support): Can you pull the provisioning audit for that group? I want to see last time we applied role assignment to affected users.

Alice Nguyen: Pasted relevant lines from provisioning audit: ```
2026-03-01T14:02:11Z INFO PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00g1abcd - changed displayName to "Billing NA"
2026-03-01T14:02:12Z INFO group-mapper: evaluated 1 mapping rules, matched 0 -> no role changes
2026-03-01T14:02:12Z WARN role-sync: members 5 flagged as orphaned from mapping
```

Diego Ramos: That log makes it clear the mapper evaluated the rule against the new displayName and didn't match. Why didn't it fall back to externalId matching?

Priya Patel: Two possibilities: (1) Their org-level config still uses name-based rules, (2) a recent deploy introduced a regression where externalId match only triggers on full-sync and not on PATCH events. I'm leaning to (2) because the code path for incremental group PATCH uses a lightweight matcher. Tagging @eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: Looking. Can you share the SCIM PATCH payload from Okta? Need to check if externalId was present in the payload or we dropped it when computing diffs.

Alice Nguyen: Payload captured from webhook: ```json
{ "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"], "id": "00g1abcd", "displayName": "Billing NA" }
``` No externalId field in the PATCH. Okta didn't send it because it was unchanged.

eng-runtime: Ah — our incremental logic currently only consults externalId when it's part of the incoming payload, otherwise it defaults to matching by name for speed. That was a deliberate optimization but it's causing this gap.

Jamie (support): Customer impact: 5 users lost billing-admin role, cannot access Billing console. They want immediate workaround and a timeline for permanent fix.

Diego Ramos: Workaround: we can either 1) force a full re-sync for that group (server-side fetch group by id, compare stored externalId, re-run mapping) or 2) temporarily add a new mapping rule for "Billing NA" -> billing-admin. Which is faster?

Priya Patel: For the short term, adding the mapping via console is quickest (~2 min) but customer will need to add rule themselves or we can apply on their behalf if they grant access. Full re-sync is safer (handles any other metadata drift) but takes a few minutes and will cause a replay of membership updates.

Alice Nguyen: Customer asked for us to do the re-sync so they don't have to update mappings. Can we run a forced re-eval of the group?

eng-runtime: We can trigger a targeted full-eval for group id 00g1abcd. I will run a job to fetch group state from our DB and re-run mapping using externalId preference (we'll use externalId if present). Scheduling now.

oncall-bot: Incident created #INC-4672 - SCIM incremental matcher skipped externalId on PATCH events. Priority: P2. Assigned: eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: Job started. Steps executed: 1) fetched authoritative SCIM group record for 00g1abcd, 2) re-evaluated mapping rules -> matched externalId rule -> assigned role billing-admin to 5 users, 3) pushed role changes to internal auth service, 4) verified access via token introspection for one affected user.

eng-runtime: Results: role assignments restored. I left a sticky note to add metrics for PATCH vs full-eval mismatches.

Jamie (support): Confirmed customer now has access. They appreciated the quick fix but want assurance this won't happen again. Requested an opt-in toggle to prefer externalId for incremental updates.

Priya Patel: Proposed permanent fix: change incremental matcher to consult stored externalId when incoming PATCH lacks externalId, OR treat group PATCH as an opaque change and trigger a full-eval if displayName changes. We'll prioritize the code change and add a feature flag to opt-in.

eng-runtime: Agree. Plan: (A) short-term config: set org flag preferExternalId=true for this org (we can flip for them today), (B) medium-term: rollout matcher change behind feature flag and run canary, (C) long-term: add observable alert when a PATCH results in 0 mapping matches but group.externalId exists. ETA for canary: 3 business days.

Alice Nguyen: Logged customer ask and proposed timeline with account team. Customer wants the org flag flipped now. Jamie/eng-runtime, can you coordinate and confirm when done?

eng-runtime: Flipped preferExternalId=true for org: 10123 at 2026-03-02T09:14Z. Verified mapping hits on subsequent PATCH. Leaving follow-up ticket: ENG-9124 (matcher incremental externalId fallback).

Jamie (support): Noted. Customer notified and very relieved. I'll close the loop. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Alice Nguyen: Thanks everyone — please keep ENG ticket updates in the thread so account team can track.

Diego Ramos: Quick retrospective note: we should document this in support runbooks: when a customer reports access loss after group rename, triage steps = check provisioning audit -> check group PATCH payload for externalId -> trigger full-eval or flip preferExternalId flag.

Jamie (support): I'll add a short KB article and link it here when done.
